sections.h2: Selling a house in Little Elm
sections.html:
You can sell a Little Elm house through an agent, on your own, or to a cash buyer who takes over the repairs. Listing tends to fetch the top price. Cash tends to mean the quickest close with the least work from you.

The town lies along Farm Road 720 where an arm of Lewisville Lake reaches east central Denton County, around twelve miles southeast of Denton. Houses here skew newer than in older Texas cities, which helps resale. Even so, a dated interior, storm damage or an inherited property can make a fast sale appealing.

An agent makes sense for a house in good condition when you are comfortable with open houses and a long wait for the buyer's loan. Going private saves the commission, but you set the price and run the contract, disclosures included. Cash fits a deadline, a lien, an estate or a long repair list.

Whichever way you go, insist that every offer be written down with the price, a closing date and a statement of who covers title and recording costs. Then take away your mortgage payoff and any back taxes to see what reaches your account.

Two projects stand out: the Hill Lane Expansion, which changes traffic near Oak Grove Parkway and Eldorado Parkway, and a 2026 asphalt street job in the Sunrise Bay neighborhood. If you live near either, be ready to explain what shoppers will see and hear.

  • Call the town's public works office to learn what is planned on your block.
  • Take exterior and drainage photos on a dry, clear day.
  • Save receipts for any roof, foundation or lake-related work.

sections.h2: How Denton County appraises and taxes a Little Elm house
sections.html:
The Denton Central Appraisal District sets values countywide. Its website covers exemptions, appeals, appraisal notices and the homestead value limitation, and owners can book time with an appraiser to talk through a number.

Texas property tax calendar for a Little Elm owner
WhenWhat happens
January 1Values are fixed
Near April 1Homestead notices arrive
April 30Usual homestead application deadline
Mid-MayProtest generally due
Around October 1Bills are mailed
End of JanuaryUnpaid taxes turn delinquent

A Little Elm bill can list the town, the county, a school district and, in some newer neighborhoods, a special district. Read it line by line.

The residence homestead exemption is the big one. Every school district must exempt $140,000 of a home's value. Seniors and disabled owners receive another $60,000, and their school tax can be frozen.

  • Any taxing unit may add its own exemption, up to 20 percent of value and never below $5,000.
  • After the first exemption year, a homestead's value can grow by no more than 10 percent annually.
  • A disabled veteran may qualify for a tiered exemption, or a total one at 100 percent.

If the house had no exemption on it, a purchase made after January 1 can still qualify for the remainder of that year. Check with the appraisal district about the paperwork needed to put the exemption in the buyer's name.

Most bills go delinquent after January 31. On February 1 a six percent penalty and one percent interest attach, and the penalty ends up at 12 percent on July 1. Anything owed comes out of your sale proceeds. Before choosing a closing date, call the Denton County tax office and ask what you owe now.

After a default notice you have twenty days to reinstate the loan, and the sale notice has to arrive three weeks ahead of the auction. Auctions happen monthly, in the spot the county commissioners designate.

Federal rules usually hold a lender back from beginning foreclosure until the loan is 120 days late. A lender that sells the house has two years to sue for any shortfall, and the borrower can ask for a fair market value offset.

If you have real equity, selling before the auction usually leaves you with more. A cash buyer can close within days and the mortgage gets paid out of the sale money.

Either kind of house can sell once ownership is settled. After an owner's death, four years are available to probate the will; a muniment of title lets heirs act on it if no administration is needed. An estate worth $75,000 or less, leaving out the homestead, can go through a small estate affidavit with court approval.

A tenant in the house means three days' written notice first, then a justice court case, then a writ of possession six days after judgment. Buyers of Little Elm homes care about the lake, the school zone and the street, and they will ask about all three.

The Denton County Clerk keeps the official records and takes your deed. A notary or similar officer has to acknowledge your signature before filing. For the current fee schedule, ask the clerk. The closing agent usually files it, leaving you to check the names and the legal description.

Call the Denton Central Appraisal District, or book an appointment with an appraiser, and ask three things. First, which exemptions are active on the account. Second, whether the homestead value limitation applies. Third, what the district needs to put an exemption in a buyer's name. The answers go in your file for the closing agent, and they help a buyer estimate the first-year bill.

Because Little Elm sits beside Lewisville Lake, buyers tend to ask about drainage, roof condition and any water history before they ask about the kitchen. Walk the lot after a rain if you can, and note where water collects. If a roof, foundation or lake-related repair was done, find the invoice and the contractor's name. Buyers see a documented repair as a problem solved, while an undocumented one looks like a risk.

Newer neighborhoods sometimes add a special district to the tax bill, and shoppers compare that line from street to street. Be ready to say what it is and what it pays for. A newer house with a dated interior or an inherited house nobody has lived in for months may sell better to an investor than to a family needing a loan.

Photographs matter too. Shoot the front, the yard and any lake-facing side in good light, and keep the files in one folder so you can send them with an offer request. Clear photos let a cash buyer give a firm number quickly instead of a vague range.

You sign the deed in front of a notary, and the closing agent then clears your mortgage, pays the taxes owed and wires you the balance. The agent then files the deed with the Denton County Clerk. Ask for the settlement sheet a day ahead and compare it to the offer you accepted. Each line should be something you expected: payoff, tax share, recording costs, any commission. A question raised the day before is far easier to fix than one raised at the table.

Keep a copy of the signed deed and the final statement. If the buyer claims a homestead exemption, they file with the appraisal district separately, so you need not follow up on it.

Start with the deed, this year's tax statement and your mortgage payoff figure, then add whatever records you have of roof, foundation or lake-related repairs. Note which special district, if any, appears on your bill. Jot down what you know is wrong with the house. If the buyer's inspector finds a problem you already disclosed, the deal rarely falls apart; a surprise is what causes trouble.

Compare offers on what you take home. A listing price minus repairs, commission and months of upkeep may land close to a firm cash number, and the cash route gets you there faster.

faqs.q: Is Little Elm in Denton County?
faqs.a: Yes. It lies in the extreme east central part of the county, on an arm of Lewisville Lake, so the appraisal district and the county clerk are both Denton County offices.

faqs.q: Does a Little Elm seller have to make repairs first?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer takes on the repairs and lowers the offer to match, so compare that number with a listing price.

faqs.q: When do Little Elm property taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31 for most bills. Penalty and interest start February 1, and by July 1 the penalty is 12 percent.

faqs.q: Does a Little Elm homestead exemption pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No, the buyer applies separately. If you never filed one, your buyer can still ask for the exemption in the year they buy.

faqs.q: How soon can foreclosure happen on a Little Elm house?
faqs.a: You have twenty days to cure after a default notice, and the sale notice comes three weeks before the monthly auction. Call the lender now and think about selling first.
